projects.title: Speeding up CNN head pose estimation with knowledge distillation
projects.summary: Peer-reviewed research: compressing a ResNet50-based head pose estimator into a MobileNetV2 student that keeps accuracy while halving inference time.

detail.heading: Problem
detail.body: Deep head pose estimation models such as Hopenet perform well but are too heavy for resource-limited devices, which restricts scalability and deployability in real-world settings like driver monitoring and online proctoring.

detail.heading: Architecture
detail.body: A teacher–student setup: a ResNet50 Hopenet teacher supervising a MobileNetV2 student, trained with relational knowledge distillation so the student learns the structure of the teacher's representations rather than only its outputs.

detail.heading: Implementation approach
detail.body: Benchmarked candidate lightweight backbones, then introduced an exchange loss function into the distillation loop - a novel contribution of the study - to alternate the supervision signal during training and stabilise the student's convergence.

detail.heading: Engineering decisions
detail.body: Optimised for the accuracy-per-millisecond frontier instead of raw accuracy. Relational distillation was chosen over response-based distillation because pose is a continuous, geometrically structured target where relative relationships carry most of the signal.

detail.heading: Results
detail.body: The distilled model reached a Mean Average Error of 3.4708 against the ResNet50 teacher's 3.4695, while per-image inference dropped from 195.9 ms to 89.9 ms. Written up as a journal manuscript.

detail.heading: Lessons learned
detail.body: Compression is an architecture decision, not a post-processing step. Also: a rigorous, reproducible evaluation harness is worth more than any single training trick - most apparent gains disappeared under consistent measurement.

projects.title: Primary Database Migration: MariaDB → MySQL
projects.summary: Application-side ownership of a business-critical production database migration, moving the primary workload from Azure MariaDB to OCI MySQL across Dev, QA, STG and PROD.

detail.heading: Problem
detail.body: The primary database supported high-volume travel search and booking workloads. Migrating from MariaDB to MySQL required more than moving data - the schema, application code, database connectivity, transaction handling, deployment environments and performance characteristics all had to be validated.

detail.heading: My role
detail.body: I owned the application-side migration, working from schema analysis and application changes through environment validation and production cutover. Infrastructure and environment setup were supported by the company's infrastructure and support teams.

detail.heading: Migration approach
detail.body: The migration was performed incrementally across Dev → QA → STG → PROD. Separate MySQL-based environments and application deployments allowed the new database setup to be validated without disrupting the existing MariaDB workloads.

detail.heading: Database & application changes
detail.body: The migration required several compatibility changes, including:
list: Replacing MariaDB sequence-based ID generation with MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT
Updating MariaDB-specific native SQL queries
Migrating from the MariaDB JDBC driver to the MySQL JDBC driver
Reviewing and improving transaction boundaries
Ensuring tables had appropriate primary keys and indexes
Updating application and database configuration for the new environment

detail.heading: Performance engineering
detail.body: Load testing in QA exposed several database and application bottlenecks. I worked on:
list: Index tuning for high-traffic queries
Precomputed summary tables for heavy reporting workloads
Application-level caching
Connection-pool migration from Apache DBCP to HikariCP
Query and database performance analysis using Performance Schema and slow-query logs
detail.after: These changes improved response times and overall stability under load.

detail.heading: Near-zero-downtime cutover
detail.body: For the final migration, the existing MariaDB database remained active while the initial data was transferred to MySQL. I developed Python synchronization scripts to capture new and updated records during the migration window and synchronize them into MySQL.
detail.after: The process also included validation and correction of AUTO_INCREMENT values to ensure data consistency after synchronization.

detail.heading: Result
detail.body: The production migration was completed successfully without major incidents, providing a stable MySQL foundation for the platform and improving database performance, transaction handling and readiness for a managed high-availability architecture.

detail.heading: Key engineering areas
detail.body: Database Migration · Backend Engineering · Cloud Migration · Performance Optimization · Kubernetes · CI/CD · Production Reliability

projects.title: Multi-hotel search logging & Elasticsearch optimisation
projects.summary: A scheduled Spring Boot service that restored full search logging on a hotel integration hub handling thousands of concurrent searches - with selective retention and batch cleanup to keep Elasticsearch stable.

detail.heading: Problem
detail.body: Tritium is a hotel integration hub handling thousands of searches simultaneously. Multi-hotel search logs were available in Kibana, but production resource constraints forced logging to be disabled to reduce Elasticsearch load. Client queries then showed those logs were essential for investigations - so full logging had to return without impacting production performance.

detail.heading: Why not built-in
detail.body: Kibana's built-in logging could not automatically filter, process and clean up logs in a controlled way, which was the critical requirement.

detail.heading: Architecture
detail.body: A dedicated Spring Boot service collecting multi-hotel search logs on a schedule, applying custom rules to selectively keep important logs while removing unnecessary ones, and processing and deleting in batches to avoid overloading the system. Packaged as a Docker image and deployed with Kubernetes manifests.

detail.heading: Challenges
detail.body: After deployment we observed high CPU usage on the Elasticsearch nodes. I addressed it with batch-wise deletion and parallel processing, query optimisation for faster execution, and Grafana dashboards to monitor CPU and performance metrics.

detail.heading: Results
detail.body: Full multi-hotel search logging with selective retention, improved observability, optimised Elasticsearch performance, and stable production operation under heavy load.

detail.heading: Lessons learned
detail.body: Retention policy is the design. Deciding what not to keep was what made the logging affordable enough to turn back on.

projects.title: Real estate price prediction
projects.summary: End-to-end regression project: cleaning noisy property listings, engineering location features, and serving predictions behind a small web interface.

detail.heading: Problem
detail.body: Listing data is noisy, inconsistently labelled and full of outliers, which makes naive price models confidently wrong.

detail.heading: Implementation approach
detail.body: Outlier removal driven by domain rules (price per square foot, bedroom-to-area sanity checks), one-hot encoded locations with a long-tail bucket, and grid-searched model selection.

detail.heading: Architecture
detail.body: Trained model serialised and served through a lightweight Flask API with a minimal front end for entering property attributes.

detail.heading: Lessons learned
detail.body: Most of the accuracy came from data cleaning decisions, not model choice - and each cleaning rule needed to be defensible, not just beneficial to the metric.

projects.title: Sports celebrity image classification
projects.summary: Classical computer vision pipeline: face and eye detection to filter usable images, wavelet-transform feature extraction, and a tuned classifier served through a web UI.

detail.heading: Problem
detail.body: Small, scraped image datasets contain many unusable samples - obstructed faces, group shots, wrong subjects - which dominate the error rate before any model is trained.

detail.heading: Implementation approach
detail.body: Cascade-based detection of face plus two eyes as an automatic quality gate, then stacked raw and wavelet-transformed features so the classifier sees both colour and edge structure.

detail.heading: Engineering decisions
detail.body: Chose classical CV over fine-tuning a deep network: with a few hundred images per class, the feature-engineering path was faster to reason about and far cheaper to serve.

detail.heading: Lessons learned
detail.body: A deterministic data-quality gate at ingestion did more for accuracy than any hyperparameter search.
